utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: It says here at the end of point 1: "The Presidency of the SFRY concluded that they should ask the Federal Executive Council to form a mixed expert commission to investigate the actual facts and inform the public." I will skip over repeating the names of these villages. In the Presidency, in addition to asking the government to form a mixed expert commission to establish this, did you deal with this issue any further?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO KOSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Please explain what degree of generality was there in dealing with issues at the level of the head of state, whether collective or individual, when such events occur.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO KOSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The level of generality is rather high, not only in situations like this one but also in many other situations. The Presidency is not responsible to investigate and establish facts, although we did have on several occasions a state commission that was established, and in several cases Mr. Bogicevic and Mr. Tupurkovski were involved. I went to Knin, they went to see Tudjman, and so on and so forth, but this was the responsibility of the executive branch of government and the responsible government organs.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In connection with this question, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff quoted from your book. I won't dwell on all the quotations she read out here, but on page 101 in your book, in a quotation that she highlighted, you mention "paramilitary formations from Sarvas threatening members of the JNA who were there as a buffer zone to prevent inter-ethnic conflicts," full stop. What are you saying here was the purpose of the JNA units?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO KOSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, the purpose of the JNA in all the flashpoints was to create a buffer zone to prevent the spreading of inter-ethnic conflicts, because the paramilitary formations of Croatia had grown considerably by that time. And had the JNA not been there as a buffer zone, larger portions of the Serbian population would have been at risk physically.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff went on to ask you something in connection with the resignation of members of the Presidency and my statement published in Politika on the 17th of March. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO KOSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do, very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: She then went on to quote me when I said I had ordered the mobilisation of the reserve forces of the Ministry of the Interior, but she didn't quote the beginning. The beginning of the passage reads as follows: "In the existing circumstances where there have been attempts to cause unrest in Sandzak and Kosovo and Metohija, I have ordered the mobilisation of the reserve forces of the security forces of the Ministry of the Interior." Mr. Kostic, where is Kosovo and Metohija, and where is Sandzak in territorial terms?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO KOSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were an integral part of the Republic of Serbia, as they still are.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Is there even a hint here of engaging any forces of the Ministry of the Interior in Croatia? And she mentioned the Knindza, and Dusan Silni, and so on and so forth. Can any connection be made here with this?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO KOSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no connection can be made. And my response to the Prosecution was that mobilising the reserve police force and employing them in Serbia fell within the competence of the President of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. I go on to say that in spite of the situation that has arisen in Yugoslavia, no emergency measures should be introduced. During the 11 years I was president, did I ever introduce emergency measures anywhere?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO KOSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware that you did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You don't have this before you, do you? You don't have this text before you?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO KOSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: It's tab 51. Then I won't quote from it any further, although in conclusion I say that I believe peace will win in Yugoslavia. Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff put it to you that you were not supported by your party as president. Do you remember that, that your candidacy for the president of -- for the Presidency as a representative of Montenegro was not supported by them? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO KOSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You showed your book here, "Deadly Manipulations." That's page 265, and you say that your name was mentioned in connection with a member of the Presidency of Yugoslavia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO KOSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And what was actually correct in connection with the quote on page 268 where Cazim Lukac expressed disagreement with your candidacy?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO KOSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Cazim Lukac was a deputy in the Assembly, and evidently those who are much better educated among his deputies got him to speak up at the session and to say that I did not recognise the Muslim people. I denied this. You can see that in my book. And I even demonstrated that Mr. Cazim Lukac didn't know whether I had ever made any such statement or where. The lady from the Prosecution does not distinguish between the two concepts of nation and nationality.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Everything that Cazim Lukac accused you of is something that you published in your book?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO KOSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, verbatim.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And why did you do this?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO KOSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did it primarily because of my conscience, but also because the Muslim people make up a large proportion of the population of Montenegro, and I wanted to show them how there was manipulation and misinformation and false information.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: On page 273, you say that the deputy, Cazim Lukac, did achieve his goal, if only briefly. He was the representative of the Party of the Democratic Coalition, and he represented himself as the only representative of Muslim interests in Montenegro, and he sowed doubt [Realtime transcript read in error "sold out"] among the Muslim and the Albanian population, and that is something that is very difficult to put right.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO KOSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I see the transcript says "sold out" and I think what was actually said was "sowed doubt."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It says he sowed doubt about my attitude towards the Muslims. He threw feathers out of a window, and feathers are difficult to collect. But in the end, feathers fall down onto the ground and end up in the mud.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: When speaking about my influence, you explained his limitations -- or my limitations because I could not convince Babic, for example. You took that as an example.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO KOSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: The same example was mentioned by Jovic in his book. And we have seen that Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff mentioned some kind of statement that I made.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown Exhibit 352, tab 79, the front page of Politika. It's translated into English.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you have this?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO KOSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 359 of what?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: It's 352, tab 79, but not from your exhibits, but it's a previously exhibited document. And this is the document from which she quoted, not from the statement itself but from Jovic's book. Do you have it now? Is that the front page of Politika?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO KOSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of the 9th of January, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, what does it say here in the subtitle?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO KOSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Open letter from Slobodan Milosevic to Milan Babic."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: An open letter published on the front page of Politika.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO KOSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And what is the title?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO KOSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The title is "The people should not make sacrifices because of the vanity and narcissism of any politician."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: The text on the ELMO is the wrong text.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What's the title of the document, Professor Kostic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This document that Mr. Milosevic is using is the original front page of Politika.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So could you read the title. Is it reply from Mr. Babic or a response from Milosevic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, it's not a reply. It's not a reply. The reply's on the other page of this document which I have. The front page says "Open letter from Slobodan Milosevic to Milan Babic," and then in large letters it says --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What Mr. Milosevic was referring to was the reply from Mr. Milan Babic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. No. I am referring to this. Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff referred to Jovic explaining what I was doing at the time, and I was actually sending an open letter to Milan Babic, and it's on the front page of Politika.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I found it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It says here in small letters under the title.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And Your Honour, you can see it on Sanction, actually.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The two letters are included in the same tab, so that's the reason for my confusion. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It's time to stop. It's actually time to stop. Did you ask a question and did you get an answer? There is no question.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, not yet. We've only just identified what she was referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff was not referring to this letter of mine but to what Jovic said in his book that I did with this letter. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO KOSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: No. We can't -- we'll have to stop now. It's time to adjourn, and we will resume tomorrow morning at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 15th day of February, 2006, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.45 p.m.,
